patch_description: The current algorithm sends every partition of data from src to each destination along the *same* single shortest path. This multiplies the cost by num_partitions and congests one route while parallel alternative networks sit idle. A better strategy: (1) only send data once over shared links — build a multicast Steiner-tree style routing where common prefixes of paths to multiple destinations are traversed only once, and (2) distribute partitions over edge-disjoint / k-shortest paths so that different partitions use different (possibly parallel) network routes, avoiding redundant transfers and balancing load. Since the BroadCastTopology records per-partition per-destination edge lists, we can assign partition i of each dst a path chosen from the k-shortest simple paths (by cost), cycling among them so no single path carries all partitions. For shared subtrees, we approximate by removing src in-edges and using k-shortest paths per dst. This reduces total cost when alternative cheap paths exist and lowers congestion.
